newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Adsteam Marine lists at A$2.62.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Adsteam Marine lists at A$2.62.

text.p: Shares in Australasian marine towage firm Adsteam Marine Ltd listed on the Australian Stock Exchange at A$2.62, a hefty premium to the A$2.00 offer price.
Adsteam Marine was spun-off from its parent company, Residual Assco Group Ltd which was renamed from Adelaide Steamship Co Ltd, with a A$160 million raising from the issue of 80 million shares.
The offer was underwritten by joint lead managers BZW Australia Ltd and SBC Warburg Australia Ltd, with Residual Assco shareholders taking a 20 percent stake in the float.
The prospectus forecast a rise in 1996/97 earnings before interest, tax and abnormals to A$24.4 million and A$26.8 million next year compared with A$23 million in 1995/96.
Shareholders would receive dividends next year, with a first half payment of six cents in April 1998 and seven cents per share in November 1998.
The Sydney-based company has a fleet of 71 tugs and represented about 58 percent of the total Australian tug fleet, as well as operations in the South Pacific region.
At 11.40. a.m. (0140 GMT), Adsteam Marine shares were trading at high of A$2.68.
Adelaide Steamship was one of Australia's largest corporate failures following the debt binge of the 1980s, coming under the control of its bankers in 1990 with debts of A$11 billion.
This has been reduced to less than A$700 million through the sale of its operations, including retailer David Jones Ltd.
